name: psql
description: Psql is a terminal-based front-end to PostgreSQL

name: -a
--echo-all
options.description: Print all nonempty input lines to standard output as they are read

name: -A
--no-align
options.description: Switches to unaligned output mode

name: -b
--echo-errors
options.description: Print failed SQL commands to standard error output

name: -c
--command
options.description: Specifies that psql is to execute the given command string, command

args.name: command
args.description: A command string that is completely parsable by the server (i.e., it contains no psql-specific features), or…

name: --csv
options.description: Switches to CSV (Comma-Separated Values) output mode

name: -d
--dbname
options.description: Specifies the name of the database to connect to

name: -e
--echo-queries
options.description: Copy all SQL commands sent to the server to standard output as well

name: -E
--echo-hidden
options.description: Echo the actual queries generated by d and other backslash commands

name: -f
--file
options.description: Read commands from the file filename, rather than standard input

name: -F
--field-separator
options.description: Use separator as the field separator for unaligned output

name: -h
--host
options.description: Specifies the host name of the machine on which the server is running

name: -H
--html
options.description: Switches to HTML output mode

name: -l
--list
options.description: List all available databases, then exit

name: -L
--log-file
options.description: Write all query output into file filename, in addition to the normal output destination

name: -n
--no-readline
options.description: Do not use Readline for line editing and do not use the command history

name: -o
--output
options.description: Put all query output into file filename

name: -p
--port
options.description: Specifies the TCP port or the local Unix-domain socket file extension on which the server is listening for co…

name: -P
--pset
options.description: Specifies printing options, in the style of \pset

name: -q
--quiet
options.description: Specifies that psql should do its work quietly

name: -R
--record-separator
options.description: Use separator as the record separator for unaligned output

name: -s
--single-step
options.description: Run in single-step mode

name: -S
--single-line
options.description: Runs in single-line mode where a newline terminates an SQL command, as a semicolon does

name: -t
--tuples-only
options.description: Turn off printing of column names and result row count footers, etc

name: -T
--table-attr
options.description: Specifies options to be placed within the HTML table tag

name: -U
--username
options.description: Turn off printing of column names and result row count footers, etc

name: -v
--set
--variable
options.description: Perform a variable assignment, like the set meta-command

name: -V
--version
options.description: Print the psql version and exit

name: -w
--no-password
options.description: Never issue a password prompt

name: -W
--password
options.description: Force psql to prompt for a password before connecting to a database, even if the password will not be used

name: -x
--expanded
options.description: Turn on the expanded table formatting mode

name: -X
--no-psqlrc
options.description: Do not read the start-up file (neither the system-wide psqlrc file nor the user's ~/.psqlrc file)

name: -z
--field-separator-zero
options.description: Set the field separator for unaligned output to a zero byte

name: --record-separator-zero
options.description: Set the record separator for unaligned output to a zero byte

name: --single-transaction
options.description: This option can only be used in combination with one or more -c and/or -f options

name: --help
options.description: Show help about psql and exit
